title: What an Allowed Claim Pays on a Pass and Trip Protection Plan
content:
What a claim pays on a Pass and Trip Protection plan is the plan's share for the event claimed on, taken of
the value at risk on the covered holding, less the plan's excess and less whatever is set against it, and it
is never below zero.

**The share.** The share taken is the plan's medical share.

**The value at risk.** The value at risk on the covered holding is the value the plan covers, taken whole.

**What is set against it.** Nothing is set against what a claim pays.

**The order the deductions act in.** The share is taken of the value at risk first, the plan's excess and
everything set against it are taken off that product afterwards, and the two deductions never act on the share
itself.

**The caps.** What is paid is then brought down to the plan's per-claim cap and held to the cover left on the
plan, which is the cover loaded onto the plan for the season less every payout already made on it, and the
result is rounded to the cent.

**The paper the payout answers to.** The payout is recorded against the paper it was assessed from, which is
the last paper accepted on the claim that evidences the peril claimed on — the letter from the former employer
on a claim made on loss of employment, the proof of a permanent move on a claim made on a permanent move, and
the doctor's certificate in every other case — and where two such papers were accepted on the same day it is
the first of them the record holds; where the claim carries no accepted paper of that kind at all, it is the
last paper accepted on the claim.

**Perils outside the cover.** Nothing is paid on a claim made on a peril the plan does not cover, the events a
plan pays out on being the ones its own list of covered perils names. A claim made on a peril the plan names
as excluded is refused whatever this rule would otherwise work out, and nothing is paid on it, so that an
exclusion beats a cover wherever a peril stands in both lists.

**Worked example (hypothetical inputs).** Take a plan whose medical share is 80.00 per cent, whose excess is
50.00 USD and whose per-claim cap is 1600.00 USD, covering a holding at 1200.00 USD, with 960.00 USD of cover
loaded for the season and no payout yet made on it. The value at risk is the 1200.00 USD the plan covers,
taken whole. The share of it is 960.00 USD. The excess of 50.00 USD comes off that product, and nothing else
is set against it, leaving 910.00 USD. That figure stands below the per-claim cap of 1600.00 USD and below the
960.00 USD of cover left, so the claim pays 910.00 USD.

**Boundary illustration (hypothetical inputs).** On a plan whose medical share is 60.00 per cent and whose
excess is 150.00 USD, covering a holding at 200.00 USD, the share of the value at risk is 120.00 USD; the
excess of 150.00 USD taken off it would fall below zero, so the claim pays 0.00 USD.
